title: The Witness of Windrow House
premise: Ivo Ishikawa, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has kept her professionally indispensable and personally invisible, is called to Windrow House when a body is found wearing clothes stolen from her own closet. The victim, it emerges, is connected to a fire thirty years ago that killed the house's original owner—a fire Ivo witnessed as a child and testified about, then buried. As she investigates, every alibi among the assembled family points back to that night, and someone begins editing her memories against her, planting evidence only she would recognize as false. At the anniversary dinner, Ivo realizes the killer is the one person who protected her all these years—her mentor, who started the fire to cover an embezzlement and has now killed again to keep his constructed identity intact; she must choose between loyalty and truth, and chooses truth, ending the cycle at the cost of the last person who ever made her feel seen.
about_author: Wendell Dunmore is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent two decades reading other people's disasters in triplicate. He writes mysteries from a coastal cottage where, he insists, nothing suspicious has ever happened.

chapters.title: The Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Called to Windrow House after a drowning, Ivo recognizes the dead man's jacket, shirt, even cufflinks—her own, taken from her flat without forced entry. The police assume she's a suspect; her memory makes her the best witness they have. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: A House That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. She surveys Windrow House for the insurer and catalogs its inhabitants: the matriarch Merle, three adult heirs, and staff preparing for the thirtieth anniversary of old Ambrose Windrow's fatal fire. A portrait's eyes seem to follow her. Beat: unease sharpening into recognition—the house matches a memory she can't place.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. She pulls the original case file on Ambrose's death and finds her own childhood statement attached, redacted. Every heir's alibi from that night was corroborated by the same witness: a young constable named Aldous Vane—now her mentor. Beat: first crack in her trust.

chapters.title: The Photographic Problem
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Interrogated about the missing clothes, Ivo reconstructs her own week frame by frame and realizes there's a four-hour gap she cannot picture—impossible for her mind. Someone drugged her. Beat: violation; her greatest gift turned into evidence against her.

chapters.title: Merle's Glass
chapters.summary: POV Merle. The matriarch rehearses her anniversary toast and privately burns a letter. She knows more about the fire than she admits and suspects which of her children is lying—but protecting the family name outranks justice. Beat: complicity dressed as love.

chapters.title: The Second Statement
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Digging into archives, Ivo finds a second child-witness statement from the fire, sealed by court order, signed with a name she doesn't recognize. The child described 'a man carrying papers out of the study.' Beat: the fire wasn't accidental—it was cover for theft.

chapters.title: Heirs and Airs
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Dinner with the heirs: charming Caspian, brittle Odile, and sullen Bram each offer alibis for the recent murder that are too polished, rehearsed in the same phrases. Someone coached them—or someone shares a source. Beat: suspicion rotating like a lighthouse beam.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: POV Detective Sergeant Okonkwo. The investigating officer's chapter: the drowned man, a private archivist, had been hired weeks ago to find the sealed statement. His notes list three names, one smudged. Beat: the investigation and Ivo's private hunt begin to converge.

chapters.title: Vane
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. She visits Aldous Vane, retired, warm, surrounded by roses. He deflects gently, reminds her he took her in after the fire, gave her a career, taught her to observe. Leaving, she notices fresh burn scars on his hands. Beat: loyalty and doubt locked together.

chapters.title: The Gap
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Reconstructing her drugged evening, she traces the sedative to a prescription belonging to Odile—who swears hers were stolen, and produces proof she was being blackmailed over an old fraud. The blackmailer's handwriting matches the archivist's. Beat: the victim wasn't innocent.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: POV Bram. The youngest heir, resentful and observant, watches the household fracture and considers selling what he knows to the highest bidder—including to the stranger who keeps asking about the fire. Beat: greed as accelerant.

chapters.title: Smoke Memory
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Under hypnosis arranged through Okonkwo, Ivo recovers the suppressed night: herself at nine years old, hiding in the hedge, watching a man carry documents from the burning study—and a second figure holding open the door. The face won't resolve. Beat: terror surfacing after thirty years.

chapters.title: The Sealed Name
chapters.summary: POV Okonkwo. The detective unseals the second statement through procedure rather than favor: the child witness was Ivo herself; the redaction was requested by Vane, citing her trauma. Beat: the protector authored her amnesia.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Cornered, Odile admits blackmail but not murder, and reveals the archivist showed her proof that Ambrose's will was forged after the fire—shifting inheritance to whoever held the originals. Beat: motive crystallizes; the money was always the point.

chapters.title: Caspian's Perfect Evening
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Caspian's alibi collapses under Ivo's timeline—he lied about the theater—but his lie covers an affair, not a murder. Yet his ticket stub places him near the archivist's office. Beat: relief curdling into new questions.

chapters.title: The Forged Will
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Comparing documents from memory, Ivo proves the post-fire will bears Ambrose's signature copied from a decades-old deed—by someone with access to county records. Only one man had both access and reason: the constable who 'found' the will. Beat: the architecture of the lie exposed.

chapters.title: An Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Vane sends Ivo flowers and a note: 'Some memories are kinder forgotten. Wear something of yours tomorrow.' She understands she's being summoned—and that he knows how much she knows. Beat: hunter and hunted exchanging masks.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV multiple, braided. Toasts are raised; Merle's speech falters on Ambrose's name; Ivo announces she has recovered her memory of the fire. Candles gutter; a door locks; the lights fail exactly as they did thirty years ago. Beat: past and present collapsing into one room.

chapters.title: The Man Who Held the Door
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the dark, Vane confesses—not to her, but to the room: he carried out the papers for Ambrose's business partner, then killed the partner and let the fire explain everything, building a life on the ashes. The archivist found the partner's ledger. Beat: confession as weapon; he's dying and wants an audience.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Vane offers her the choice he's always offered: silence, protection, belonging. He reminds her she owes him her whole self. Ivo, voice steady, recites his crimes from memory—every date, every detail—and hands him to Okonkwo. Beat: the theme made flesh; truth chosen over love.

chapters.title: After the Ashes
chapters.summary: POV Merle. The matriarch signs the true will's restoration, dissolving half the estate to charity, and dismisses the household with unexpected grace. She tells Ivo the house never deserved their silence. Beat: power relinquished before it corrupts completely.

chapters.title: The Witness of Windrow House
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Weeks later, Ivo testifies cleanly, declines Vane's one letter unread, and donates the dead archivist's ledger to the record. Walking away from Windrow House, she realizes invisibility was a cage, not a shelter. Final beat: identity reclaimed—she remembers everything, including herself.
